hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We stayed at the St. Regis Bora Bora for five nights, and it was an unforgettable experience. From the moment we arrived at the Bora Bora airport, everything was incredibly easy. A St. Regis host was waiting for us, helped with our luggage, and within about 15 minutes we were on the boat heading to the resort. The resort itself is absolutely beautiful. We stayed in an overwater villa and loved having our own space, the views, and especially the ability to watch the sunrise from our bed or our lanai. Our villa was one of the last villas along the property, so there was quite a bit of walking or biking to get to the main areas. We actually loved riding the bikes around the resort, but if walking or biking is difficult for you, I would recommend requesting a villa closer to the main resort area. One of our favorite routines was having coffee delivered around 6:00 AM. My husband would take his morning swim while I enjoyed the sunrise. The resort was so peaceful early in the morning. We also loved simply spending afternoons riding our bikes, relaxing at the villa, and enjoying the property. We took the complimentary boat/bus over to the main island one afternoon to visit town, which was a nice break from resort life. The Spa Is a Hidden Gem: One of our favorite discoveries was the St. Regis spa. For approximately $35-$50 per person, you can use the spa for either a half day or full day. The spa is located in the middle of the resort's lagoon, and the snorkeling there was incredible. We originally booked the half-day option from 9:00 AM to 1:30 PM, but enjoyed it so much that we extended it to a full day. We were practically the only people there for much of the morning. You have access to the lagoon, loungers, easy water entry, steam room, sauna, jacuzzi, showers, and other amenities. It was one of the most beautiful and relaxing areas of the entire resort. Dining: We had dinner reservations at the different restaurants throughout our stay and enjoyed watching the sunsets around the resort. The biggest surprise for us was the cost of food and drinks. Everything was very expensive, and several other guests commented on the prices as well. I'm not particularly a foodie, however we enjoyed the breakfasts and were happy with our dinners. Service: The service throughout the resort was exceptional. Everyone we encountered was kind, helpful, and always greeted us with a smile. Our butler also made our departure very easy. He had our boarding passes and arranged our boat transfer back to the airport. Before leaving, we managed to get in one last snorkel and bike ride around the property. Overall: The St. Regis Bora Bora gave us exactly what we hoped for - beautiful surroundings, an incredible overwater villa, excellent snorkeling, peaceful mornings, and plenty of opportunities to simply relax.
review_title: St. Regis Bora Bora — Beautiful Resort & Unforgettable Stay

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: I've done the Conrad in the Maldives along with two other properties in the Maldives. I loved it, BUT the level of attention to detail at the St. Regis Bora Bora is unbeatable. Bora Bora is already amazing and the St. Regis brought the magic of this island to another level. Location: This resort doesn't feel like it impedes the natural environment. Rooms: From what I've heard, the St. Regis has the largest overwater bungalows in French Polynesia. We stayed in the beachside villa. Value: This is a top tier luxury resort. You will pay a good amount of money to be here. However, you absolutely will get what you pay for. Meals and drinks can be expensive if you don't do at least half board, but everything is expensive in all of French Polynesia. Cleanliness: The staff, butlers, everyone kept the entire property spotless. Noise level: Apparently the St. Regis was FULLY BOOKED at the time of our stay. At no point did it ever get loud from our neighbors or anyone else. Butler Lydia was amazing, and the Beach Boys worked hard to make the stay easy. St. Regis Bora Bora, my heart aches to be there again ASAP!
review_title: Already planning a longer stay ASAP!

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Lovely stay! The entire resort staff was excellent and very attentive and welcoming. Truly top tier hospitality. Beautiful rooms, peaceful and private stays. Chloe took excellent care of us and we enjoyed the morning coffee and tea services immensely. The location is an easy trip from the Bora Bora airport and the atmosphere is incredibly relaxing. We spent a ton of time swimming near our bungalow and at the lagoonarium. It was fairly busy season, but didn't feel crowded. The resort arranged some really nice scuba diving for us. We did a half day at the spa and it was perfectly relaxing! Clean facilities. The major area for improvement is the food. The staff were excellent, but the Bamboo restaurant especially needs to be reworked. It was somehow our most expensive and most mediocre dinner. Vegetarian options were lacking, but that seems to be the trend in French Polynesia. Even main fish dishes at Bamboo were disappointing. The Lagoon restaurant and bar however were a highlight. Overall, still a lovely five star stay.
review_title: Excellent hospitality; room for improvement with the food

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: The St. Regis Bora Bora is a magical place! My wife and I have stayed at many wonderful hotels, and St. Regis Bora Bora is the best of them all. We spent a week there to celebrate our 5th wedding anniversary. The Lagoon Restaurant was a special dining experience, and the sunset views at the 727 Bar cannot be beat. The beach is well-maintained. The adults-only Oasis Pool was very quiet and serene. We also enjoyed tennis, dance lessons, and fishing. Our overwater villa was spacious, well appointed, and clean. Our Butler, Lydia, went above and beyond. It's hard to imagine any hotel being better than the St. Regis.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: The St Regis is a beautiful property on an island near the mainland of Bora Bora. We stayed at this hotel upon the suggestion of Pacific For Less. It was a magical visit, from the snorkeling, to the food, to the service, and the beautiful cottage on the water. It was a perfect place to celebrate an anniversary!

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We spent an absolutely magical stay at St. Regis, and we could not be more satisfied. This resort is the very definition of perfection and undoubtedly deserves 5 stars! From the moment of our arrival, we were welcomed by an incredibly cheerful, kind, and professional staff. Our butler, Diana, was fantastic! On our anniversary, she surprised us with a chocolate cake. Our overwater bungalow was simply fantastic! Being woken up in the morning by coffee delivered to the bungalow terrace was the icing on the cake. The lagoonarium is of indescribable beauty. As for the food offered by the resort, it was delicious, with fresh and tasty dishes celebrating local flavors.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Our second trip to this fabulous resort arranged by our agent with Pacific for Less was no less exceptional than our first time. The St. Regis commands a beautiful space on the motu. This is where you go for top quality service where everyone knows your name. The service throughout is exceptional but the butlers and restaurant staff really make sure you have everything you need. And Pacific for Less got us an extra night, special perks, booked all our excursions and dinners, re-did our flight so we could arrive earlier, and sped us through customs at the airport.
review_title: An exceptional trip with special perks

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: My husband and I celebrated our 25th anniversary at the St. Regis after first spending several nights at the Hilton Moorea. The grounds were well kept, the staff very friendly and welcoming. Everyone greeted us by name! Our butler Chloe and her trainee Arthur were extremely warm yet professional; they informed the restaurants of our many food allergies. Our overwater bungalow was very impressive. Sadly, other than breakfast and the Aparima grill, we found the food at the resort disappointing; which is why this isn't a five star review. The flavors were very muted despite high prices. The biggest letdown was our private candlelight beach dinner - entrees were inedible, undercooked risotto was crunchy and bland. Far Niente, the Italian restaurant, was also sadly a miss - marinara tasted like tomato sauce out of a can. We also had an issue with a restaurant charge on our last day - the charge on our final invoice was more than the actual restaurant check; when I brought this up, it was poorly handled and they never responded after saying they would look into it.
review_title: Trip of a lifetime with some misses.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: This isn't just a hotel, it's a magical place with the most special people in what is arguably one of the most beautiful places on earth. After 11 visits it has become a home away from home for us and our daughter. This is made especially true by the friendly smiles and hugs we get from our friends Temaiana, Reuben, Matira, Teva and others, and this year also by Lydia our butler. As a family, being surrounded by exquisite beauty but also the exemplary service, restaurants and activities this resort offers makes it difficult to go anywhere else.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We enjoyed 10 nights at St Regis Bora Bora as a couple. We'd love to visit again. So much to do - great views, lots of water sports, great snorkling, lots of wildlife trips. The hotel has a fabulous lagoon for easy and safe snorkling. We did helicopter tour, sunset cruise, speed boat hire and snorkling, glass bottom boat tour and jeep safari. Lots of relaxing time, beach and pool space. Nice rooms. Good restaurant choices. Service very good throughout. We had great butlers called Diana and Chloe. Food was good although one of our party was vegetarian and choices were somewhat limited. Rooms clean and well maintained. We never felt it was too busy.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Such a beautiful resort. Seamless arrival and departure - picked up by speedboat from the airport. We were upgraded to a huge overwater bungalow. The entire resort is stunning. The staff is incredible. It never feels even a bit crowded although it was nearly full. There is a cat named Regis that is sort of the mascot! The resort is large and there is a lagoon area with lots of fish to snorkel in.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Our stay in Bora Bora was supposed to be the trip of a lifetime. Unfortunately, while we were there, we got the call that my mother had been rushed to the hospital back in the U.S. The way the staff responded is something I'll never forget - the GM and entire team were incredibly kind, compassionate, and understanding, helping us figure out travel plans. Before everything happened, we had already been blown away by the resort itself - absolutely beautiful, service second to none.
review_title: Beautiful Resort with a beautiful staff

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: The property is wonderful. Villas spacious and beautiful, views magnificent. The resort is large so prepare to walk, bike, or call for a golf cart ride. The concierge is very on top of things, suggested an activity based on my interests, and worked hard to secure a guide for a hike. Staff in general very attentive and friendly.
review_title: St Regis Bora Bora - highly recommend

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: When we started doing our research on where to stay in Bora Bora for our honeymoon, we landed on the St. Regis through our travel agent Pacific For Less. We stayed 5 days and had an incredible experience. Our bungalow was spacious with direct lagoon access. The resort provided free bikes. All staff incredibly friendly and welcoming. White glove service.
review_title: You Will Not Want To Leave

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: One of the most beautiful stays of my life. The resort is exceptional. The atmosphere is incredibly peaceful, luxurious, and relaxing. The rooms are huge, elegant, and very comfortable. The lagoon is absolutely breathtaking - turtles and stingrays almost everywhere. Special thanks to Charlotte, Hélène and butler Jenna.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We stayed 3 days at the beautiful St. Regis Bora Bora in a Lagoon overwater villa. Very spacious, featuring bedroom, large bathroom, livingroom and outdoor space. Butler service one of a kind - fresh morning coffee to the villa. Food absolutely amazing, loved the Lagoon & Bamboo restaurants. The resort has a marine biologist and lagoon conservation activities. Beach beautiful too. Level of service the highest we have experienced in Bora Bora. Resort feels calm at all times, no crowds. Booked a 2-tank dive, saw manta and leopard rays.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: I am sure there are places in French Polynesia equally as beautiful as St. Regis. The food is very good and our beach side villa with pool is large and comfortable. I did not expect the level of service that our butler Lydia provided.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We had spent the first 7 days of our trip at the Conrad (see separate review) and I had gotten incredibly sick while at the Conrad - diagnosed with cholecystitis (gallbladder inflammation), needed medications and medic assistance, essentially did not leave the room for over 72 hours. Despite being SO sick, no one at the Conrad really seemed to care. The GM at St Regis was aware of my medical situation and personally greeted us on arrival along with the assistant GM, immediately got me a medication refill at no charge. This personalized service was emblematic of our entire stay. We were in Bora Bora for our 10 year wedding anniversary and whereas the Conrad didn't even recognize it, we got several different recognitions throughout our 5 night stay at the St Regis.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We loved our 4-night stay. Our Overwater Bungalow with island views was absolutely amazing, and resort amenities exceeded our expectations - Lagoonarium, gym, beach and pool all first class. Perfect location with breathtaking views of Mount Otemanu. Booked through Pacific For Less.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We chose the St. Regis Bora Bora for our honeymoon. One of the main reasons we selected St. Regis over The Four Seasons was its reputation for exceptional service, and it exceeded every expectation. Special thanks to butler Mila. Some of our favorite moments were spent relaxing on the crystal-clear lagoon outside our overwater bungalow.
review_title: From Bucket List to Best Vacation Ever!

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Our second visit to Bora Bora, chose St. Regis due to past experience at St. Regis Maldives and Bonvoy brand loyalty. Booking/check-in smooth. Facilities expansive but walkable. Dining: only Lagoon restaurant stood out as fine dining; Bamboo dinner was a complete failure - 45 minutes from seating to appetizer, sushi quality on par with cheap grocery store sushi, staff shortage apparent. Butler service was much more reactionary and impersonal than St. Regis Maldives - services provided 'on request' via phone call rather than anticipatory, no WhatsApp. Overall wonderful time despite some flaws in restaurant management and butler service falling short of 'anticipatory' billing.
review_title: A Worthy Luxury Resort for a Terrific Bora Bora Visit!

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: It is incredible... the beach has the best colors, the facilities, everything is very tasteful, excellent food, it is wow.
review_title: The best hotel in Bora Bora.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: This place is amazing. Starting with Laure, our butler - gracious, thoughtful and caring. Along with colleague Julian, we were well taken care of. Water color, warm temperature and clarity are true to the pictures.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Stayed 4 nights in a beach side villa with pool facing the lagoon. Butler Emma took us on a tour on arrival. Villa huge with own pool and hammock. Breakfast good but the only gluten free items on the buffet were bread - no pastries/cakes/biscuits or cereal/granola, could ask for pancakes/waffles to be made. Saw no marine life outside the hotel's private lagoon. We started at Bamboo but I wasn't feeling well, cancelled mains after starter arrived - staff only charged for the starter, exceptional service. Found the Italian restaurant most limiting for gluten/dairy free - just pasta and tomato sauce, didn't even bring gluten free bread which was a little disappointing. Asked for late check out but couldn't stay in our room (booked for new guests) - they moved our luggage to another beach villa for us to use until our transfer, no charge. Suggestions: refillable water bottles/water stations to cut plastic, more gluten free breakfast items, a washing line in the bathroom for wet swimwear. Would highly recommend the beach villa over the water bungalow given very little marine life to spot.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: A true once in a lifetime experience. Location breathtaking, rooms/restaurants/pools/beaches immaculate. Staff exceptional - warm, attentive, professional. Special thanks to Jenna. Tip: skip the Private Beach dinner, book dinner at the lagoon restaurant instead.
review_title: The St Regis is a true ONCE in LIFETIME dream resort.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: This resort is amazing. Staff goes over and beyond. Villa was perfection. I only wish there were more food options for lunch. Definitely visit Bamboo for dinner more than once, best food on the property.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Beautiful resort with top notch service. Booked through Pacific For Less. Perfect stay, excellent cuisine, gorgeous setting and overwater bungalow.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Second trip to St Regis, for our 32nd anniversary, upgraded to royal suite. Hostess Chloe took care of everything without delay. Pool guys worked hard, servers/bartenders learned our favorite drink after the first day. Food at all restaurants 5 star caliber. Couples massage at the spa.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Second trip to French Polynesia, organized wedding with small group of family & friends via event planners Maria then Pauline. Had a lagoon view OTW bungalow 303 - room huge, though probably needed some plumbing renovation. Private dinner at Lagoon restaurant was gourmet and delicious. Wedding ceremony at the spa was magical, though very hot.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: I almost cried when we had to leave, it's just paradise. Leandro was such a great butler, Emma was really nice too.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: A beautiful and perfectly located complex. Resort staff seem to have come into the world in a good mood. Perfect 5-star luxury. Received a beautiful upgrade. Probably the highest luxury level you can climb in French Polynesia.
review_title: A superlative experience - better than holidays

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Our stay was exquisite, didn't want to leave. Overwater bungalow well furnished, resident sea turtle under our bungalow visible in the floor window. Bed ultra comfortable, AC worked amazingly. The food was overpriced, but there were a few different options on site.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Deluxe 1 bedroom over water villa with Mt Otemanu view, worth every penny. Villa large, comfortable, huge open shower, 2 person soaking tub. No ceiling fans (looked like there had been fans once). Housekeeping good but a bit late in the day. Bikes were heavy, one-speed, geared high - hard to pedal, switched to golf cart. Booked through Costco with meal plan - breakfast buffet good but not fantastic, fresh fruit selection disappointing in variety/quality. Best meal at Bamboo (Asian). Alcohol very expensive, ~$25/drink; $90 t-shirts, $75 caps in the boutique. The resort lost its Forbes 5 star rating this year - villa was showing some wear, scratches on wooden floors, worn flooring. Service and grounds full 5-star level though - staff knew us by name after day 1. Zero complaints overall, highly recommend.
review_title: Pretty hard to improve on this experience

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Came from staying at the Westin for a week. First part of stay over the water, wonderful room. Pool was nice but one day was over-run with small children being allowed to run amok, filling bar stools and sitting on the bar (inappropriate parenting). Second portion moved to island lagoon mountain view land villa, their absolute favorite. On 4 occasions had to contact butler regarding other guests entering their private grounds - after the last and most intrusive incident staff put up a 'PRIVATE' sign and the Head Butler came to speak with them. Restaurants very good except the French restaurant - elevated Polynesian French, did not enjoy at all, plus children running amok in this 'fancy' restaurant using tablets with sound on. Was during Chinese New Year, lots of guests for the holiday whose kids caused the villa intrusions and restaurant disruption - 'quite a bunch of entitled people'. Grounds and service outstanding, they really take care of you ('The Four Seasons could take some lessons'). Also stayed at Westin and Four Seasons same trip.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Stayed late Feb-early Mar 2026. Butler Aleandre superb. Over-water unit beautiful, meticulous, exceptional service. Food very good with french twist - helps to know some french. Food at the resort off the charts expensive. Free shuttle once per day into the main island for groceries/snacks - mini fridge in room. Booking as a package through a travel agent yields benefits and reduces cost.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: First trip to Bora Bora, exceeded expectations. Butler Jenna made dining reservations for every night, checked on them regularly. Property very exclusive but large, walking not ideal - bikes provided or golf cart pickup. Spa day: massage and pedicure excellent. Dining pricey but portions extremely generous, shared entrees to save cost. Reef side garden villa 2700 sq ft, private pool on patio. Surprise birthday cake left by butler. Insider tip: bug spray necessary, had over 15 mosquito bites within one day dining outside at night.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: [Chinese language review] Stayed with family, butler Laura (French) was professional and patient, helped book restaurants, checked on them daily, gave son small gifts. Check-in/out smooth, everyone very kind, may return.
review_title: We had an absolutely wonderful stay at The St. Regis with my family

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: The best hotel I have ever stayed in: wonderful paradisical location, fabulous service, warm and welcoming staff, outstanding cuisine.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Celebrated 35th anniversary, 2nd visit back to St Regis after trying Le Bora Bora and the Intercontinental. Grounds immaculately kept, top notch customer service, personal butler brings French Press coffee to the OWB each morning. Villas large with huge bathrooms, housekeeping twice a day. Restaurants lovely, loved Lagoon and Aparima Grill nights. Breakfast buffet pastries didn't seem to get restocked once popular items ran out. Sad that Tahiti Nui airlines is discontinuing direct flights from Seattle to Papeete.
review_title: If Paradise Had A Nickname, it Would be St Regis

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Stayed 3 nights Intercontinental Thalasso, 5 nights St Regis, 1 night Four Seasons - St Regis offered the best experience overall. Beachside villa with own pool, land crabs outside. Impressed with Far Niente (Italian), server Olivia from France excellent. Butler service felt a little choppy - butler there 3 of 5 days only in afternoons, different people brought coffee on different days, got confusing for tipping, but phone requests were always handled. Lagoonarium a must see. Pastry chef amazing, best buffet of the 3 places visited. Acknowledged Titanium Bonvoy status; got room for $750/night including tax vs listed $3400/night rate via points redemption.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Been to Bora Bora 13 times, hadn't been back to St Regis for years - forgot what was missing. Service and food unmatched at other properties (planned to check Westin in September). Everyone remembers you by name, personal concierge a nice touch. Large room and varied dining important here. Shark/ray tour and scuba dive recommended. International flight delayed 12 hours - one call to travel agent Pacific for Less and all domestic details were adjusted.
review_title: Still my favorite after staying at most of the big brands

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: This was our fourth trip to French Polynesia, with previous stays at Four Seasons, Pearl Resorts (Taha'a and Tikehau), Hilton Moorea, InterContinental Thalasso, Sofitel, InterContinental Tahiti, and Hilton Tahiti—so we have a strong basis for comparison. Cons: Severe food poisoning during our stay, which significantly impacted our experience. Grounds were subpar for a five-star resort and not well maintained. Our private plunge pool was unusable for an entire day without warning or explanation, and no one seemed concerned. The Executive Assistant Manager did not follow through on commitments, requiring us to repeatedly follow up ourselves. Butler service was inconsistent and unreliable—more akin to a basic concierge than true butler service. Food quality overall was disappointing. Pros: The Lagoonarium was a pleasant surprise—better than the snorkeling experienced in Tikehau and far more accessible. Staff were consistently friendly and pleasant. The fresh mahi-mahi at lunch was a standout and one of the few food highlights. After six nights at the St. Regis, we transferred to the InterContinental Thalasso for the remainder of our trip and were pleasantly surprised. The food, responsiveness, grounds, and overall experience were all noticeably better. Unfortunately, this stay did not meet expectations, and we will not return to the St. Regis.
review_title: Disappointed in Our Stay at St. Regis Bora Bora- Will Not Return

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We flew to Bora Bora from Raiatea on Air Tahiti. A nice group of St. Regis' team met us at the airport and collected our luggage. It was a lovely boat in which to ride to the hotel. Nice reception at the hotel upon arrival. Our overwater bungalow was a nice, expansive room. Lots of drawers, closets, and storage but also a lot of wear and tear. Yet, you don't really notice because the room is so large. The Lavazza coffee machine makes excellent coffee. The bed is very nice as are the linens and towels. Room HVAC is excellent. Deck and chairs and side view of Otemanu are excellent. But, the room refrigerator was empty. Nothing in it. I must order drinks a la carte? That is odd for St. Regis. Fill the refer and let me consume it when I want. We walked out on our deck barefoot but didn't notice that the deck was sandy. Without doormats, we tracked sand back into the room. The sand in the room annoyed us and we couldn't find a broom. It took three phone calls, and three hours, to get help with clean-up. The deck should have been swept before we checked in. Having a butler was nice, at first. But we would later wonder why we had one. Almost every question to the butler was referred to the concierge. And the butlers change with little warning. There is no real, meaningful connection with the butler, even over a five-day stay. At our first breakfast, it took three requests to get coffee. I asked for a Caesar salad with REAL (traditional) Caesar dressing; I received a dry salad with mayo and garlic in ramekins on the side. For one of our gluten-free meals, we got a poke bowl that lacked any sauce. No flavor. A spaghetti dish also fell flat. The hotel removed some charges after we complained about these meals. Overall, the food was generally good, but we would not say it was excellent. Anton was a top-notch waiter who helped us with our gluten-free (Celiac) meals - should be training the rest of the staff. For cocktails, Jeremy and Aaron were great bartenders, but the hotel lacks ingredients for a good Manhattan (no high-end sweet vermouth nor Luxardo cherries). At the 727 bar, a staff member tried to remove my unfinished glass without asking. A manager in a blue shirt aggressively confronted me for yelling 'arret!' to my cart driver when I urgently needed a ride back for my insulin - a really strange encounter. There is a dearth of tropical fauna in the sea around the hotel, worse than other Tahitian hotels - the hotel lagoon feels more for kids, an unnatural human-made environment, not worth staying at St Regis just for the lagoon. The hotel's bikes are tired and poorly maintained, and golf carts don't always slow for cyclists - a collision risk. Housekeeper Tatiana was a great asset. In summary, mostly service and encounters with some staff kept us from rating St Regis four stars. Our food allergy was well tended to throughout our stay. The breakfast pastries are the best we've had in decades.
review_title: Some service issues, but great care for Celiacs. Decent rooms showing some wear, some great staff, some not so great.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: The best hotel I have ever stayed in : wonderfull paradisical location, fabulous service, warm and welcoming staff, outstanding cuisine. My heart simply warmes when I think back on my stay. I will come again for sure.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We had an amazing stay here with our 3 kids (7/9/12). The service was unbelievable, the OWV were huge and comfortable, I can't say enough great things about this place. We had a late flight out of Bora Bora and they gave us a beach villa to use for the afternoon after we checked out. Every little thing was perfect.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: A big thank you to the entire St-regis team for this incredible moment. Special thanks to Monoihere from bar 727 for his exceptional hospitality. Thank you also to Lea and Aaron of the aparima for their kindness and professionalism. And a huge thank you to Charly, Maite and Laetitia from Bamboo: we were very well served, always caring with us during the meal. A great team that really makes a difference. We had a great time and will be back with pleasure.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Our stay was absolutely incredible. I have traveled to many tropical islands and locations and they all pale in comparison to Bora Bora. The St. Regis resort is nothing but spectacular and feels almost surreal to be on the same planet! From the thoughtful staff (shout out to our butler Julian who was phenomenal), to the breath taking views, and even the Lagoonarium which was the most phenomenal snorkel experience I have ever had. I cannot recommend this stay enough.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: The St Regis on Bora Bora was STUPENDOUS in very way. It was one of the most beautiful and special places I've ever been. You are greeted at the airport by the hotel staff and taken by boat through the beautiful blue waters of Bora Bora to the resort. The overwater villas are extremely spacious, immaculate and absolutely gorgeous. The resort has a tennis court, well-maintained. They have a gorgeous very large Lagoonarium where you can snorkel without booking a special excursion. The beach staff attended to your every need. Hiro was our concierge and created a complete itinerary. The food at all the restaurants was amazing. Our butler Oceane was gracious, kind and utterly delightful. From start to finish every single detail of the St Regis Bora Bora was pure excellence.
review_title: St Regis Bora Bora - STUPENDOUS in every way!

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Dream resort for many years - the region and the property lived up to the hype. We were lucky to have stayed during the Christmas holiday. Service: World-class professionalism and friendliness exhibited by the staff. Laure and Chloe were impressively attentive. Nuuvai and Kennie at the concierge were exceptional. Staff across the resort were always friendly. The food was thoughtfully crafted. Highlight was the Italian restaurant and the vodka rigatoni. The villas were spacious and well placed. Overall, the stay was wonderful.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: What a wonderful experience at this resort. From the moment we checked in Maxene at the front desk was awesome. We were then greeted by Emma our lovely associate who did an amazing job. She made our anniversary SO special with a surprise cake in our room. Ameretti, Karen and Lola were fantastic at the breakfast buffet and ensured my son's nut allergies were taken care of. Resort itself was gorgeous and what truly made it unique was the fabulous staff and awesome customer service. We spent 5 days here and not a day went by where we were not happy about something.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: TLDR: We absolutely loved our stay at the St. Regis and are counting down the days until we can return. I don't think I'd want to stay anywhere else! The Lagoonarium is a unique feature and the Butler service is incredible (especially Oceane). The service overall is the most high quality, attentive service I've ever experienced. My mom and I decided to stop in Bora Bora for 4 nights on our way to a wedding in Fiji. Our butler Oceane greeted us and took us on a tour of the hotel property. The over-water bungalow was absolutely amazing, incredibly spacious with all amenities. Activities: flower crown making, champagne sabering, tennis, snorkeling in the Lagoonarium, coral cutting & planting, jet ski tour, scuba diving. Overall, the staff are incredibly kind, gracious, and attentive. Standout meals: Pizza Moana at Bamboo, Ahi Tuna Poke Bowl. We stayed in early December during the rainy season, only little spurts of rain. Apply a lot of sunscreen. Don't buy floaties - the Beach Boys have spares.
review_title: A once-in-a-lifetime trip I hope to experience again.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort delivers the experience of a lifetime! Ideally situated on the lagoon, the views of the lagoon and the mountain are stunning, any time of day. The property is expansive, providing space for a family to engage in water sports, tennis, outdoor and indoor fitness, excellent dining, and sightseeing activities. The staff is extraordinary in their commitment to deliver the highest level of service to their customers. They are warm, engaging, and always working to anticipate our needs, beginning with the personal concierge and front desk, but including the poolside team, servers, and housekeeping! Insider tip: the beachside villas face the rising sun and have views of the adjacent islands. Bicycles provide convenient transportation on the property.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: The rooms are clean, very good and great aromatics. The kids are very nice and the staff agnes and jeaneth too kind very nice with the kids. (Machine translated review.)

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Having travelled extensively in multiple luxury resorts all over the world, my expectations were muted as there is a lot of build up on how amazing this destination is. The build up is real. This was one of my top 5 experiences in my travels. We stayed in the 2 bedroom Royal Villa and it was amazing. Perfect views, very spacious and the decor lovely. My only complaint was the lack of a mini bar. When you are dealing with guests that are on time changes, etc there should be an option to purchase food/drinks in the room without bothering room service. They also don't give access to a ton of water. Silly little things, but a premium room such as this should come with an abundance of water and options for snack in the room. The food was excellent, the service we received from our breakfast host each day was a highlight. Please try the Bora Mary. Our butler Mena was incredible - a true gem.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We stayed at the St. Regis Bora Bora after transferring by boat from the Westin. Given its reputation as one of the top resorts in the world, we arrived with high expectations. In many ways, the property and experiences are incredible. In others, it fell short of the standard it claims. Check-in was surprisingly underwhelming - lobby crowded, our luggage was misplaced for about 15 minutes, we were sent to a dim changing area to dig through bags. Overwater bungalow: huge, elegant, breathtaking view, but clear the bungalows are due for a proper refresh. Several window latches broke off as soon as we tried to open them. The floor was very creaky. The water closet had a musty smell. Most upsetting, I opened a drawer to grab a bathing suit and found a large cockroach on my clothes - extremely unsettling at this price point, spent the rest of our stay obsessively checking luggage. Only small plastic Evian bottles instead of reusable bottles. The lagoonarium is a highlight, Napoleon fish Moana greeted me. Surprised to learn two large lemon sharks near the restaurant and some OWBs are fed daily by staff to keep them around - made several couples nervous about swimming off their bungalows. Food quality on property generally very good. Service felt inconsistent - resort as a whole felt understaffed, later confirmed by an employee. Golf cart drivers zipped around paths quite fast, constant rushing and stomping on floors at Lagoon restaurant was a bit jarring. The butler service felt more like a mobile concierge than a classic dedicated butler experience - butlers were constantly on the phone and seemed stretched thin. Special experiences (sabrage, romantic beach dinner, canoe breakfast) really shine. Overall: spectacular setting and unforgettable experiences, but underwhelming arrival, maintenance issues, pest incident, and sense of understaffing prevent calling this a flawless ultra-luxury stay.
review_title: Gorgeous setting and memorable experiences, but not quite the flawless ultra-luxury stay we expected

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: My husband and I returned to the St. Regis Bora Bora and it was just as amazing as we remembered. So many fond memories from our honeymoon a few years ago, and new ones made during this trip. We booked with Claudia from Pacific For Less this time. We loved eating at Lagoon and grabbing a pre-dinner drink at 727 Bar and watching the sun set each night. Oceane was our butler and was fantastic; even going above and beyond by giving us a stuffed turtle (honu) to take back home to our son who absolutely loves turtles. The Beach Boys were always smiling and so attentive. We took advantage of the great onsite gym and snorkeling in the lagoon. Cannot wait to return again!

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We would like to express our sincere gratitude to all the staff at St. Regis Bora Bora for your remarkable hospitality and thoughtful attention. Your professionalism and kindness made our stay exceptional. Thank you for this memorable experience. Thank you to Boyan, Nina, Jenna our Butler and Delphine.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Bora Bora is spectacular. The St Regis makes it more so. We stayed 7 nights in an overwater bungalow lagoon side. Two huge rooms, enormous bathroom, windows all around to gaze at the blue water. Coffee delivered in the morning at a time of your choosing. A few very minor cons: food was generally just okay. Skip the Lagoon restaurant with an 'up charge' - our least favorite meal. Astronomical drink prices. Unstocked mini bar. Butler service was spotty - our seriously charming butler forgot several requests we made. Would we go back? In a heartbeat.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: I just returned from a five-night stay at The St. Regis Bora Bora. The resort grounds are phenomenal, and the level of service and staff quality is what makes this property stand out. My butler Marion did a fantastic job. The concierge team is outstanding. The overwater bungalow is nice and spacious, though showing its age - some wear and tear here and there, would benefit from upgrades especially the AC and bathroom. I enjoyed all my meals - Bamboo and Fariente offered the best value for money. I had the signature six-course tasting menu at Lagoon, which left me unimpressed - all right but nothing to remember (except the mashed potatoes) and not worth the money IMHO. One minor comment regarding the restaurants would be the lack of a true immersive dining experience - the setup of Fariente and Bamboo is a bit underwhelming, just a few tables near the pool area, limited decor and music. The staff were consistently great.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: Expectations were high for this trip after everything we've heard and researched about the St. Regis. The resort was beyond anything we could have imagined and hoped for. The service is impeccable. Our butlers, Mina and Diana, thought of every deal to make our anniversary trip an unforgettable experience. Alice, our housekeeper, did a fabulous job. And the food - wow! Lucie at the Lagoon and Ta'pau was darling and so gracious. The variety of excursions offered, the ease at which to do anything you want, the views, the size of the bungalows, everything exceeded our expectations.
review_title: Stop your research and book the St. Regis!

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: My family and I just returned from the St Regis Bora Bora and we are all having withdrawals from the perfect trip. We were a group of 16 and everyone at the St Regis went out of their way to make us feel welcome. The rooms we had were great and worked perfectly for our large family group. Sarah and Diana (our butlers) were very attentive and helpful. We had a fair amount of children with us and the hotel went above and beyond to baby proof the rooms and fence off the plunge pools. The rooms themselves were very comfortable with great air conditioning. While the bathrooms show their age a little bit, they were still nice and perfectly adequate. The bikes provided were a game changer (we have previously stayed at the 4S next door and they could really benefit from adding bikes). The restaurants were all great. What really makes this place special is the people.

hotel: The St. Regis Bora Bora Resort
review_text: We just got back from our 2nd trip to the St. Regis Bora Bora (celebrating our 5 year anniversary) and it was just as beautiful as we remembered from our honeymoon in 2020. Five-star service from start to finish by the St. Regis staff. Oceane, our butler, was fantastic and went above and beyond. You definitely can't write a review on this resort without giving a huge shout-out to The Beach Boys; Temaiana and Vida. Ruben was amazing as well. We told ourselves we'd come back every 5 years, but I honestly think every two years sounds a lot better.
review_title: Twice as Nice: Our Second Trip to St. Regis Bora Bora
